answer: An agent economy can require each identity to lock a scarce token for a fixed period before it may submit jobs or earn reputation. Rewards accrue only to the same locked address, while misconduct can slash its deposit, so splitting one operator across many aliases does not multiply trustworthy history for free. The attacker must buy and immobilize capital per identity, accept exposure to penalties, and wait through the lockup; like timber committed to a voyage, each stake is an anchor that raises the cost of flooding the system with disposable agents.
